bib.title: SELF-DISCOVER: Large Language Models Self-Compose Reasoning Structures

read.skipped: Fig. 10 meta-prompt text is garbled glyphs in the extraction and could not be read; figure values read from extracted chart labels.

question: Can an LLM compose, per task and without labels, a reasoning structure from atomic reasoning modules that beats fixed prompting such as CoT at lower inference cost?
hypothesis: Each task has a unique intrinsic reasoning structure, and composing several atomic reasoning modules into it beats applying a single a priori module such as CoT.
contributions: SELF-DISCOVER, a two-stage zero-shot framework (SELECT, ADAPT, IMPLEMENT at task level; follow the JSON structure at instance level)
Gains over CoT and Plan-and-Solve on BBH, T4D and MATH with PaLM 2-L and GPT-4, with 10-40x less inference compute than self-consistency or per-module voting
Evidence that discovered structures transfer across models (PaLM 2-L to GPT-4, GPT-4 to Llama2-70B and GPT-3.5) and resemble human structures

method.summary: Stage 1 (once per task) runs three meta-prompts on a model: SELECT useful modules from 39 seed reasoning modules given a few unlabeled task examples, ADAPT them to the task, IMPLEMENT them as a JSON key-value reasoning structure (with one human-written example structure from another task). Stage 2 appends the structure to every instance and the model fills in the values to reach the answer. Evaluated zero-shot against direct, CoT, Plan-and-Solve and ensembling baselines.
method.task: zero-shot prompting for complex reasoning (BBH, T4D, MATH)

datasets.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
datasets.split: all tasks; number of examples per task not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Models told to end with 'Thus, the final answer is [X]'; heuristics designed per task by manual inspection of outputs to extract answers

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.size: 200 examples subsampled from the test set
datasets.preprocessing: Extracted answers manually sanity-checked and annotated for all methods; instance-level structures generated via one-shot demonstration

other.MATH: a PaLM 2-L with stronger instruction tuning is used for MATH

other.note: zero-shot meta prompting Llama2 gave low-quality structures, so GPT-4 structures were used

inference.samples: Self-Discover: 1 call per instance plus 3 task-level meta-prompt calls; CoT-Self-Consistency samples 10 per instance; majority voting over 40 reasoning modules (inferred: 39 listed in Table 2, text says 40 RMs); number of runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot. Stage 2 prompt: follow the JSON plan, then the structure, then the task instance. Stage 1 uses the few task examples without labels (number not stated; Appendix E humans were given 3). Llama2 used zero-shot; GPT-3.5 geometry used 3-shot demonstration of structured reasoning.

metrics.name: accuracy / exact match
metrics.definition: final answer extracted from 'Thus, the final answer is [X]' compared with gold

metrics.name: inference calls per instance
metrics.definition: number of LLM calls needed per instance

baselines: Majority voting of each reasoning module
Best of each reasoning module (oracle labels)
eval.protocol: Single reported accuracy per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Efficiency comparison on only 2 BBH tasks (movie recommendation, geometric shapes) with GPT-4.

prompts.purpose: Stage 2: solve instance with discovered structure
prompts.text: Follow the step-by-step reasoning plan in JSON to correctly solve the task. Fill in the values following the keys by reasoning specifically about the task given. Do not simply rephrase the keys.

results.note: Equals the T4D GPT-4 gain over Plan-and-Solve (85-53) per Sec 4.1; vs CoT it is 85-52=33; Fig 1 and intro give other figures (up to 42%).

limits: Evaluated only on BBH, T4D and a 200-example MATH subsample; MATH gains are small and computation errors dominate.
Authors concede longer input and output than CoT/direct, increasing cost per call.
Llama2-70B could not produce good structures itself (footnote 3).
No seeds, variances or significance tests; number of unlabeled task examples for Stage 1 not given; decoding settings not given.
Efficiency comparison covers 2 tasks only; answer extraction used manual per-task heuristics.
Tied to Oct-Dec 2023 model versions; gpt-4-turbo-preview and PaLM 2-L are dated.
